Definition: to be filthy, i.e. (intensively) to loathe, pollute
BiblicalUsage: Abomination is a word for what God loathes, and for what He will not loathe. The law says ye shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creepeth, and Moses commands Israel to utterly detest the abomination and not bring it into the house. The psalm turns the word toward mercy, for He hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what God calls abominable I must loathe, and what God will not abhor I must not despise. The creeping thing and the afflicted man are the two poles of the word, and the cross is where they meet. My position is that the afflicted are never an abomination to God, even when the world treats them as one.
